newsitem.title: JAPAN: Perry in Tokyo to complete Okinawa agreement.
newsitem.headline: Perry in Tokyo to complete Okinawa agreement.

text.p: U.S. Defense Secretary William Perry arrived in Japan from the Middle East on Sunday to conclude an agreement on reduction of the U.S. military presence on Okinawa, a move galvanized by the 1995 rape of a Japanese schoolgirl by three American marines.

Under the agreement, pushed by both governments to end one of the most contentious issues between Washington and Tokyo since the second World War, the United States will return some 12,000 (4,856) of the 58,000 acres (23,473 hectares) now used by the U.S. military on the Japanese island.

The agreement, including key changes in U.S. Marine Corps training and flight operations and reduction of aircraft noise, is expected to be announced at a news conference on Monday attended by Perry and U.S. officials and by Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda and Defence Minister Fumio Kyuma.

Perry stressed on his arrival that the agreement, negotiated over the past year, would reduce the U.S. military intrusion on the lives of Okinawans but would not diminish American and Japanese in either Okinawa or elsewhere in Japan.

The highly visible and noisy presence of the U.S. military on Okinawa has for decades drawn "Yankee go home" protests from islanders. Those objections rose to a fever pitch after the rape of a 12-year-old schoolgirl by three U.S. servicemen on Okinawa 14 months ago.

The agreement will not significantly reduce the 28,000 U.S. troops on Okinawa and would not mean any reduction in the 47,000 American soldiers, sailors and airmen in Japan, which both governments agree are a key to stability on the Pacific rim.
